Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

remote adjective

far away, out of the way

also remote place, isolated, out of the way, far-off, distant, if it’s not too much out of the way for you

classical

Caes. BG 7.1: silvestribus ac remōtīs locīs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 7.20.2: remōtō locō (Lewis & Short)

remōtus, remōta, remōtum

remote, out of the way, secluded

The participle of removeō: moved away, so far off and private; with ā, away from (cīvitās ā cōnspectū remōta, Cic. Verr. 2.3.85).

Other words

  • longinquus, longinqua, longinquum — far-off, distant

    also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 47: ex locīs tam longinquīs (Lewis & Short); Tac. Ann. 2.24; Traupman 203

    Distant in space, and in time long-lasting; from far away is ex longinquō (see far).

  • dēvius, dēvia, dēvium — out of the way, off the road

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.4: id et nōbīs erit perjūcundum et tibi nōn sānē dēvium (Lewis & Short s.v. et); Traupman 111: sī tibi nōn sānē dēvium erit

    From dē viā, off the road.

Examples

  • ut quis ex longinquō revēnerat, mīrācula narrābant, vim turbinum et inaudītās volucrīs, mōnstra maris, ambiguās hominum et bēluārum fōrmās, vīsa sīve ex metū crēdita

    whoever came back from far away told of marvels: violent whirlwinds and unheard-of birds, sea monsters, shapes half human and half beast, things seen or believed out of fearTac. Ann. 2.24

  • Per tēlescopium videntur remōta ut proxima.

    Through a telescope remote things look close at hand.Comen. OP 79

See also far, remote control.
